title: Holes, Voids, and the Words Around Them

sets.relationshipLabel: a worker and the tool of their trade
sets.explanation: A diver reaches for a flashlight and a climber reaches for a rope — each explorer paired with the gear that defines the job.

sets.relationshipLabel: a hollow landform necessarily has this structural part
sets.explanation: Every pit has a rim and every basin has a floor — the part is not optional, it's what makes the hollow a hollow.
baitTags: basin could suggest a taxonomic landform type

sets.relationshipLabel: a geological process and the non-karst result it necessarily leaves behind
sets.explanation: Collapse leaves rubble and dissolution carves a channel — each process named by its plain physical aftermath, not by a fancy cave-type name.
baitTags: channel could suggest a watercourse-type landform, pulling toward the taxonomic set

sets.relationshipLabel: a kind of large karst feature, more specific type
sets.explanation: A cenote is a specific kind of sinkhole and a grotto is a specific kind of cave — the general term hiding a named subtype.

glossary.definition: a deep natural pool of water surrounded by rock, formed where ground collapses to reveal groundwater below
